title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting, inferred from the neighbouring pages: G is a group scheme over S, apparently SL_2 or a related form. The neighbouring pages use Tr and det, a centre μ_2 and a rank-2 object E'. ρ and σ are fixed sections of G, and ρ(α) denotes conjugation, so αρ(α)^{-1} = αρα^{-1}ρ^{-1} = [α,ρ]. In this conjugation notation (17) unfolds to (18) on the next page: τστ^{-1}σ^{-1} = ε.

On p.311 Grothendieck sets up a morphism (α,β,μ,ε) ↦ ((ξ,η,μ),ε) from the group G^*_{ρ,σ} to 𝔛_{ρ,σ}×μ_2, with ξ = [α,ρ] and η = ε[β,σ]. The fibre over a section ((ξ,η,μ),ε) is the scheme of solutions of (15a) αρ(α)^{-1} = ξ and (15b) βσ(β)^{-1} = εη.

This page shows that these fibres have points, by producing explicit solutions.

1. The isomorphism B'_0 ≅ H_{ρ,σ} (B'_0 apparently a subgroup scheme, perhaps Borel-like) gives a privileged solution α = u of (15a). It is characterised as the unique solution that is a section of B'_0. Morally this is because T_α ∩ B'_0 = {1}: the solution set of (15a) is a torsor under the centraliser T_ρ, and B'_0 is transversal to it.

2. By construction this same u satisfies uσ(u)^{-1} = η, not εη.

3. To correct by the central sign ε, he tries β = uτ (16). Then βσ(β)^{-1} = u·τσ(τ)^{-1}·σ(u)^{-1}.

4. Suppose τ satisfies (17): [τ,σ] = τσ(τ)^{-1} = ε. Since ε is central, βσ(β)^{-1} = uεσ(u)^{-1} = εuσ(u)^{-1} = εη, which is (15b).

So the problem reduces to finding τ with τστ^{-1}σ^{-1} = ε, i.e. τ conjugates σ to εσ. The next page shows this forces τ to normalise the torus T_σ. Since Tr(εσ) = εTr(σ), solvability for ε = -1 requires Tr σ = 0 when 2 is invertible. Conversely, Tr σ = 0 gives the 'numerical conditions' for ε to be a commutator [τ,σ].

The purpose is to show the map G^*_{ρ,σ} → 𝔛_{ρ,σ}×μ_2 is surjective (fppf-locally) and to understand its fibres as torsors, in the study of the 'loop equation' for SL_2-type groups.
errors: No mathematical error. The computation σ(β)^{-1} = σ(τ)^{-1}σ(u)^{-1} and the use of the centrality of ε are correct.
Minor slip in the manuscript: a stray closing parenthesis in 'uεσ(u)^{-1})'.

ideas.what: Correcting a particular solution of a twisted-commutator equation [β,σ] = εη by a central sign, writing β = uτ with [τ,σ] = ε
ideas.modern_name: Torsor/fibre analysis of commutator maps; twisting by elements conjugating σ to -σ

ideas.what: A privileged solution of [α,ρ] = ξ, unique among sections of a transversal subgroup B'_0 (since T_α ∩ B'_0 = 1)
ideas.modern_name: Canonical section of a torsor via a transversal slice (Borel/unipotent slice to a torus)

ideas.what: In SL_2, σ is conjugate to εσ (ε = -1) only if Tr σ = 0, and then τ normalises T_σ (next page)
ideas.modern_name: Trace conditions for conjugacy in SL_2; normaliser of a maximal torus

deep.surprise_reason: This is a routine algebraic step: correcting a particular solution by a central sign within a larger, unpublished study of the 'loop equation' for SL_2-type group schemes. Nothing here is new to a specialist.
transcription_corrections: 'pour trouver une solution (15b) de ce une solution de l'équation' should read roughly 'pour trouver une solution (15b) de l'équation βσ(β)^{-1} = εη'.
'qui soit [-...-] section de B'_0' reads 'qui soit [crossed-out word] section de B'_0'.
In the last displayed line the image shows 'βσ(β)^{-1} = u εσ(u^{-1}) = ε uσ(u)^{-1} = εη', with u written over crossed-out μ.
In (16) a μ is overwritten by u in the image: 'u τσ(τ)^{-1}σ(u)^{-1}'.
